scope.read: Nine Corus basic_english, detail_english and basic-unit en/covered/proof/required metadata, with the unchanged prewritten oracle and its exact supplied pair facts.
scope.not_read: Other cohort prose, final snapshots, journal, new execution logs, product source or test source.
scope.price_rule: A typed role-level exchange/loss description plus any independently stated captures can preserve the price without spelling out every SAN. Proof-only endpoints and mere SAN occurrence do not themselves describe a capture or require all endpoint events in the basic answer.
scope.selection_rule: Coverage of the prewritten primary question is separate from a closed useful local question. Missing a different future event is not a price omission unless it changes a claim actually selected into the basic answer.
scope.quality_rule: A closed subanswer can be present inside a poor basic explanation. Presence of that part is not treated as passing the full short, focused, natural-basic release criterion.
scope.delivery_rule: The original v9 decoder failures are parent-reported execution findings, kept separate from the semantic content present in this frozen backend reading. These are not independently observed browser failures in this assessment.
scope.after_freeze_changes: Parent reports later action_moves/serializer/consumer reference-contract repairs preserve the original v9 English text, selected content, facts and progress. This report assesses the preserved v9 content and does not substitute a new product run.
scope.finalization: All nine cases finalized. No new source/prose/log reading, engine replay, oracle revision or additional verification was added during finalization beyond the assessment/oracle files needed to preserve links and counts.

findings.conclusion: The role-level Material prices already preserve important actual exchanges in 03, 05 and 09 without a separate sentence for every SAN. Requiring all capture SAN strings would falsely report omissions and reintroduce event-list pressure.

Two selected basic gains have actual other-square prices only in details: cxb5/Rxe3 in 01 and Qxb7/Rxb2 in 04. These are selected-content closure failures, separate from what primary question was chosen.

02's later original-knight removal, 08's absent Nd7 exchange question, and 11's absent alternative a-pawn retention are genuine primary scope gaps. They are not automatically important price omissions of every narrower instantaneous evasion, clearance or first pawn exchange actually asserted in basic.

03 and 09 largely preserve their primary chess answer, but independent histories, temporary relations and scattered account sentences hide the answer. The remaining problem is content admission and ownership/grouping, not primarily sentence syntax.

10 states the real early transposition and preserves the common bishop-for-knight price. Longer-arm endpoint trades stay in details and are not falsely claimed as root-move consequences. The duplicated exchange narration is redundant, not a missing price.
08 has a valid short Bd7 rook-clearance explanation but gives the played Nd7 only as a root SAN. A closed local mechanical answer must not be reported as completing the frozen central comparison.

02 and 05 have parent-confirmed original v9 decoder failures from reading endpoint proof as actual capture. Frozen prose still needs content grading, while actual delivery is failed separately. The reference audit's absence of Corus issues does not prove ownership semantics or frontend execution.

limits: This report does not mark the whole phase-one release complete, and does not infer an overall 18-case score from this nine-case subset.

A registered auxiliary match, a useful primary subquestion and an unlisted mechanical observation are counted separately. Their presence does not automatically turn the whole unfocused basic into a good short answer.
Price closure is evaluated for selected claims and exact observed episodes, not for every capture in the final provided ledger.
No unsupported evaluation cause, forced threat, universal safety or terminal-result claim was found in the nine basic texts. This does not certify such claims in unexamined product outputs.

No clear subject/verb or syntactic grammar failure was found. Repetition, ambiguous same-SAN actors, friendly support described as targeting, and weak hierarchy remain substantial English presentation issues.
Parent handles separate typed-source owner validation. This assessment does not assert the source caller responsible for the identified semantic omission.
Current attacks, temporary doubled pawns and retained pieces are read at their stated source occurrence; they are not silently upgraded to permanent states or causal engine judgments.
No engine, corpus rerun, product patch, oracle revision or actual browser inspection was performed for this assessment.
The counts are distinct, overlapping diagnostic categories. A primary semantic closure, registered auxiliary closure, or local mechanism is not summed into an overall product-quality pass rate.
reference_resolution: Per-judgment arm/offset refs include their exact line_id. Offsets are zero-based facts paths[].steps indices; occurrence/SAN/original-current identity are resolved in the linked SHA-frozen facts. Full moves and all evidence are not copied here.

primary_semantically_useful_and_complete.definition: The unchanged primary chess comparison is meaningfully conveyed with required prices, even if distributed across basic fragments. This is not a whole-basic readability or release-pass count.

registered_auxiliary_useful_and_complete.definition: At least one useful closed auxiliary question prewritten in the unchanged oracle. This overlaps the primary count and is not added to it.

closed_subquestion_of_primary_without_fu.definition: Useful complete subquestion of the unchanged primary, not a replacement primary or a post-hoc oracle success.

unlisted_closed_local_mechanism.definition: An observed local mechanism absent from the prewritten success questions. Recorded separately and not promoted to a primary/registered-auxiliary pass.

important_selected_claim_price_omissions.definition: Same supplied source contains a reply/loss price that changes an actual basic gain claim and is only in details. No requirement to narrate all PV captures.

primary_not_selected_or_organized_bounda.definition: Selected basic scope misses the same-original-target answer in 02, substitutes a different mechanism in 08, and preserves primary content without selecting it as the central flow in 09. These are not three extra price omissions.

unsupported_cause_threat_or_resolution_c.definition: Explicit unsupported causal, forced-threat, permanent-safety or resolution claim found in this nine-case basic reading.

clear_syntactic_grammar_failures.definition: Clear syntax or subject-verb error found by this LLM reading. Zero does not mean idiomatic, unambiguous or readable English.

material_center_dilution.definition: Histories, transient relations or scattered price fragments materially hide the selected comparison. No character-count threshold is used.

material_repetition.definition: Substantial repeated targets, supports, survival histories or standalone descriptions; semantic price closure is judged separately.

moderate_repetition.definition: Correct bounded comparison retains duplicate exchange narration.

mild_repetition.definition: Small repetition in an otherwise short answer, which may still have a scope failure.

parent_reported_v9_decoder_failures.definition: Original v9 actual frontend reference-contract failure reported by parent: endpoint proof interpreted as actual capture. Not independently observed here and not substituted for content grading.

parent_reported_additional_engine_budget.definition: Actual additional investigation budget failure reported by parent. The admitted finite comparison is still assessed, without expanding into a stronger verified evaluation claim.
